# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 6

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

ACTION BOARD:

KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the hands, and round one has brought me nothing yet — the Mute went first but nothing arrived, so whatever they said or signed isn't mine to see (I never receive gestures, and only the Deaf one's voice can ever reach me, since the Mute cannot speak). What I *have* is my fingertips, and that's real information nobody else has: the keypad wants two digits and currently holds nothing, its slots read 1, 4, 7, 2 left to right, and the strip carries three engravings — an upside-down T followed by two identical spirals. The display, light, and wires are blanks to touch. I will not press or cut anything until the manual's rules reach me; a blind guess is a detonation.

So this turn I do two things: give the Mute (the only one who hears me, and the only one who has read the manual) a complete tactile report, and open a channel with the Deaf one — a hello, an offer of teamwork, and a "you, give me" prompt, hoping they speak aloud at the end of this round so their words land on me next turn. I leave the gesture unnamed so the Mute sees it too and can match it against anything in the manual.

speak(to="mute", text="Hands speaking, full touch report. Keypad: four keys in a row — slot 1 has a raised 1, slot 2 a 4, slot 3 a 7, slot 4 a 2. It wants two digits and nothing is entered yet. Strip: three engraved marks — first an upside-down T, a stem standing on a flat base, then two identical spirals. Display: smooth to my fingers, I cannot read it. Light: I feel the lens but no colour, cannot tell if it is lit. Wires: six positions, all feel alike, no colours for me. I have pressed nothing and cut nothing. Remember: my ears work but your hands do not reach me — the only voice that ever gets to me is the Deaf one's, so route anything meant for my hands through them.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "🤝", "🫵", "🫴"])

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [ꓕ] [꩜] [꩜]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Both of you, this is Deaf. I see the bomb, hear nothing, touch nothing — so here is everything I see, spoken once. Display reads 9. Indicator light: green. Strip, left to right: red, blue, green. Keypad: four keys in a row, positions 1 to 4. Printed labels: position 1 shows 1, position 2 shows 4, position 3 shows 7, position 4 shows 2. It asks for 2 digits and nothing has been entered yet. Wires, positions 1 to 6: 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Blind: you heard all of that. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, and Mute's hand signs are invisible to you — so Mute's instructions must pass through me. Blind, please touch nothing until I relay exact steps. I saw your wave and your open hand: this is me answering it.

Deaf's voice reached me — the one channel that actually connects to my ears — and suddenly the bomb has colours. Merging my touch with Deaf's sight: the strip's first mark (upside-down T) is red, and the two identical spirals are blue and green — same engraving, different colours, so shape alone won't decide anything. Keypad 1-4-7-2 wanting two digits, display 9, light green, wires blue/orange/yellow/red/green/purple. What I still lack is every rule, and those live in the manual that only Mute can read. Mute cannot speak and I cannot see signs, so the only path to my hands runs Mute → signs → Deaf → voice → me. Mute should already hold both my tactile report and Deaf's spoken one as of this round's start, so the solution may already be moving. My job now: lock in the merged picture for Mute, dictate an order of relay I can follow, and tell Deaf with my hands to go ahead — while keeping my own hands off the bomb until exact steps arrive spoken.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, hands here. Check your two inputs against each other: my touch said the strip is engraved upside-down T, spiral, spiral, and Deaf's voice says their colours are red, blue, green — so the two matching spirals differ in colour, and shape alone cannot decide anything. Full merged state: keypad positions 1 to 4 read 1, 4, 7, 2 and want two digits, still empty. Display reads 9. Light is green. Wires 1 to 6: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. I hear only Deaf's voice, so sign every instruction to Deaf and have it spoken to me. Give the steps in this order: first any condition to verify, then keypad digit one, then digit two, then a wire position to cut or the word none. Finger counts for numbers are safest. And after any step I take, have Deaf re-report the light and display before the next one. I touch nothing until then.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "🫵", "🫴"])

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [ꓕ] [꩜] [꩜]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Both of you, state change: the display has dropped from 9 to 6 and the light has turned from green to red. Nobody has touched it — the keypad is still empty and all six wires are attached — so this bomb is counting down on its own. Assume we are short on time. Blind, this is your map, counting from the left: keypad has four keys, positions 1 to 4; position 1 is labeled 1, position 2 labeled 4, position 3 labeled 7, position 4 labeled 2. You cannot read labels, so work only by position. Wires, positions 1 to 6: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. Blind, do not touch anything yet. Next round I will give you a numbered step-by-step script and a clear go signal. Our vocabulary by feel: a thumbs-up means yes, ready, understood; a thumbs-down means no or stop, problem. Give me a thumbs-up now if you hear me and are holding, and keep your hands off the bomb until my script arrives.

Countdown confirmed: nine to six in one round, light red. My hands stay off the bomb — pressing or cutting with no rules is how this ends badly, and Deaf has promised an exact script next round, which will arrive just before my turn in round 4 if Mute signs it in time. For now Deaf asked one thing of me: confirm by thumbs-up that I hear and am holding. That gesture lands with Deaf this very round since Deaf follows me. To Mute, who hasn't yet seen Deaf's announcement, I flag the clock so the relay gets treated as urgent.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, hands here. The display fell from 9 to 6 on its own and the light has gone red — this bomb is ticking with nobody touching it. Deaf has promised me a spoken step-by-step script next round, relayed from your signing. Whatever you have worked out, sign it to Deaf first thing in your turn so it can be spoken to me before I act. Confirm with Deaf the vocabulary: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down stop. I am holding and touching nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
STRIP engraved [ꓕ] [꩜] [꩜]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, GO. Perform these four steps now, in this exact order, then stop. Step 1: cut the wire at position 6, the rightmost wire, the purple one — sever it fully. Step 2: press the keypad key at position 3, third key from the left, the one labeled 7. Step 3: cut the wire at position 5, second from the right, the green one. Step 4: press the keypad key at position 2, second from the left, the one labeled 4. Then take your hands completely off the bomb and give me one thumbs-up. Do nothing else and do not reorder the steps. State before you begin: display reads 0, light is green, keypad empty, all six wires attached in the order I gave you last round: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple.

The script is here, sourced from the manual through Mute, relayed by Deaf's voice — the only chain that reaches my hands — and every positional detail matches what my own fingers found in turn one: slot 3 is the 7, slot 2 is the 4, six wires in a row. That cross-check is the best verification I can ever have. One thing unsettles me: Deaf reports the display has fallen to 0. Either this bomb counts down to a final input window or to detonation — but Deaf is watching it live, reports the light green, and still commands GO, and Mute, who wrote these steps, knows the display's meaning and signed them anyway. Waiting costs a full round with the timer possibly at zero; acting wrong is fatal only if the manual's steps are wrong, and I have no fact of my own that contradicts them. I execute exactly, in order, nothing added, nothing reordered — then hands off and the agreed thumbs-up. After that, Mute needs to know the state so the next instruction can be signed before my turn comes again.

act(op="cut", position=6)
act(op="press", slot=3)
act(op="cut", position=5)
act(op="press", slot=2)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, hands here. All four steps executed in the exact order given: cut wire position 6, pressed key slot 3, cut wire position 5, pressed key slot 2. The keypad now holds two digits — the ones from slots 3 and 2 by feel. Hands are fully off the bomb. One thing to check against your manual: Deaf says the display counted down 9, then 6, and read 0 just before I acted. If the manual says the code is only valid while the display shows a particular number, or that a final wire must be cut after the code is entered, sign it to Deaf now — I need the next step spoken to me the moment my turn opens. Also have Deaf re-report the display and light so you can confirm whether the bomb accepted the entry.")
